research_question: Formalize a live-validation decision framework for the current 6-strategy portfolio
universe_searched: The current 6 strategies only (no new instruments)
major_findings: GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED scorecard built; thresholds derived from each strategy's own historical max streak, not current losses; rejected an arbitrary '3rd-loss=pause' rule for CADJPY ARB
major_exclusions: No new candidates searched -- this phase built the evaluation framework, not new strategies
methodological_limitations: Live sample sizes of 2-9 trades per strategy, far below any statistically confident threshold

research_question: Diagnose the current portfolio's TRUE factor/regime/correlation structure
major_findings: Zero New York exposure; HIGH volatility is the portfolio's only net-negative regime; correlation RISES on the portfolio's worst drawdown days; correlation-adjusted effective N=2.67 of 6 (vs naive HHI 5.19); JPY concentration not proven to be the dominant cause (mechanism/session at least as implicated)
major_exclusions: No new instruments tested -- purely diagnostic on the existing book
methodological_limitations: Trade-level correlation not meaningful for this book (used daily/weekly instead); GBPUSD Monday's session label is a data artifact, not a true classification

research_question: Rank which diversification CHARACTERISTICS would actually help, via calibrated synthetic archetypes (not real strategies)
column9: Factor importance ranking: HIGH-vol compatibility (7.87R) > drawdown-correlation (5.46R) > mechanism diversity (14.7R swing, separate ablation) > normal-day correlation (0.85R, smallest); every archetype tested, even the best, deepened nominal portfolio drawdown on average even while improving total R
column10: No real strategies backtested -- explicitly diagnostic/synthetic, disclosed throughout
column11: Single-draw noise found and corrected mid-phase (rebuilt to 300-draw averaging); currency ablation could not cleanly isolate currency from its assumed correlation effect
